messages:
Maria G.: quick brain-dump — i've been prototyping a slot-credit based congestion control for the continuous batcher. goal: smooth enqueue spikes without hard eviction storms.

Maria G.: rough idea: each tenant gets a credit bucket (credits ~= tokens representing ability to enter inflight batch). credits regenerate at a configured rate. when a request arrives we debit credits by cost(request). if insufficient credits we either queue to a shadow backlog (cheap) or route to slowpath workers. this avoids immediate drops.

Maria G.: pseudo:
```
credits[tenant] = min(cap, credits[tenant] + rate*dt)
if credits[tenant] >= cost(req):
  credits[tenant] -= cost(req)
  admit_to_batch(req)
else:
  append_shadow_queue(req)  # lightweight metadata only

# periodically try to drain shadow queue when credits free up
```

Alex P.: interesting. how do you measure "cost(req)"? tokens? seq_len? logits?

Maria G.: tokens * model_cost_factor mostly. plus a small overhead for streaming requests (they hold slots longer). tuneable multiplier per model.

Samir: curious about starvation — if a tenant ramps credits regen low, shadow queue could grow unbounded. are you proposing TTLs or dynamical priority?

Maria G.: yes TTL + ageing. two knobs: shadow-ttl (drop after x seconds) and ageing-score that slowly increases priority for older entries so we don't starve small long-running tenants. also a per-tenant soft-cap on shadow size that triggers fallback to dedicated slowpath.

Jordan: runtime visibility question: can we observe instantaneous credit balance + shadow queue depth cheaply? that's been a blindspot for ops.

Maria G.: this is where i prototyped an eBPF probe on the enqueue path to sample per-tenant enqueue_age and credit_balance histograms. lightweight counters from kernel tags so we don't allocate heavy objects in hotpath.

Tess: eBPF sounds neat but ops/security will ask about surface area. we should limit to aggregated metrics (per-pool, not per-tenant full traces). also helm chart must make it optional.

Liam: also want to see how this interacts with kv-cache. if we admit more requests via soft-queue, we might overflow kvcache headroom and cause evictions. any eviction signals planned?

Maria G.: plan: integrate eviction hooks — when kvcache headroom < threshold, we auto-throttle regen rate (feedback loop). basically credits regen is dampened by cache_pressure signal.

Samir: feedback loops are risky. need hysteresis and rate limits on adjustments or we'll get oscillation.

Maria G.: agreed — add a PID-ish controller with clamped adjustments and a cool-down window (5s). also we expose a debug endpoint to force regen scaling for experiments.

Alex P.: question on consistency: if we run many runtime instances, where are credits tracked? central store = single point of failure, local only = split-brain. hybrid?

Maria G.: hybrid: approximate local credits with occasional reconciliation. local fast-path decrements local token pool and emits a usage delta to aggregator. aggregator does slow reconciliation and can apply global damping (e.g., cap per-pool total). worst-case we conservatively reduce local regen until reconverge.

Jordan: that seems pragmatic. we should add a stat for "stale-credit-corrections" so we know how often local guess differs.

Tess: telemetry: besides enqueue_age and depth, capture dequeue_jitter (time between scheduled send and actual send) and admission_latency. ops wants a chart of shadow->admit conversion rate.

Maria G.: noted — will add metrics names: batch.credit_balance, batch.shadow_depth, batch.enqueue_age_p50/95, batch.dequeue_jitter_p95, batch.shadow_admit_rate.

Liam: runtime-bot posted a canary deploy last week; any experiment flags for this? we can't flip it across all customers.

Maria G.: runtime-bot: I've added a feature-flag gated rollout: rollout.by_pool and rollout.by_tenant tags. default off. canary pool = internal dev/pilot customers.

runtime-bot: canary deploy scheduled at 2025-11-07T22:00Z for pool dev-canary. notifying oncall. :bell:

Samir: fallback behavior: if the whole continuous-batcher is saturated (regen clamped low) do we automatically fall back to single-request workers or drop?

Maria G.: fallback to slowpath workers with optional priority token (so we don't route all traffic to slowpath). also provide a hard-drop policy for noisy tenants when a config flag is set. default favor slowpath + drop after shadow-ttl.

Alex P.: few more nitty bits: 1) ensure admission decision is idempotent for retries, 2) add a small per-req fingerprint in shadow queue to dedupe obvious duplicates, 3) avoid blocking on reconciler RPCs in hotpath.

Maria G.: yes idempotent admission planned (sticky request id), dedupe heuristics (same fingerprint within 200ms). will make reconciler async and best-effort.

Tess: can you drop a short RFC note with diagrams and config knobs? ops and security need to review before canary.

Maria G.: i'll draft RFC. next steps in thread: what telemetry dashboards to create for canary, exact config defaults, and security checklist for eBPF.

Jordan: for the RFC include a small simulation (python) showing arrival bursts and how credits + shadow queue behaves vs current hard-slot model. numbers sell this.

Maria G.: will do. thanks all — i'll post a link to the RFC draft and the canary feature-flag once it's ready. :rocket:

Tess: :thumbsup:

Liam: nice work, excited to see metrics.

runtime-bot: deploy-canary event: feature-flag batch.slot-credit enabled for pool dev-canary at 2025-11-07T22:00Z
